newsitem.title: UK: Galen jumps to premium on LSE debut.
newsitem.headline: Galen jumps to premium on LSE debut.

text.p: Shares in pharmaceutical company Galen Holdings Plc leapt to a 19-percent premium on Thursday on their first day of dealings on the London Stock Exchange, dealers said.
Galen shares, issued at 150p, jumped 28-1/2p to 178-1/2p by 0935 GMT in volume of 4.7 million shares, making it one of the heaviest-traded stocks in London.
Dealers said demand from institutions, and particularly investors in Ireland, boosted the shares in the Northern Ireland-based company.
The company raised around 30 million stg from a placing and said it would use the proceeds to expand its existing businesses and to fund acquisitions.
Galen is one of the largest manufacturers in Northern Ireland and employs about 600 people.
It manufactures and markets prescription medicines which are sold in the UK and Ireland via a salesforce of around 50 representatives and contributes to about 75-percent of the company's turnover.

Galen's pharmaceutical products business involves the research and development of new ways of delivering drugs, notably an intravaginal ring (IVR) which can release more than one drug at a prescribed rate inside a patient.
The company's other main business - ethical pharmaceutical services - provides clinical trial services to other pharmaceutical companies.
Galen made pre-tax profits for the year to September 30 1996 of 7.2 million stg against 3.6 million stg for the previous year.
In the current year, the company said it made pre-tax profits of 5.4 million stg for the six months to March 31.
